verdict.rationale: Highnote's agentic-commerce page names this use case: it issues cards per agent via API, auto-closes them when the workflow ends, and enforces merchant category restrictions, per-transaction caps and velocity limits at authorization. Spend-rule docs back the MCC and dollar-amount controls. However, merchant locking is shown only at the category level, and expiry appears only as workflow-end auto-close rather than a configurable expiry date. missing for 10: documented single-merchant locks, explicit configurable card expiry, hands-on or independent corroboration of the agent-card flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an agent its own card — issue a scoped virtual card to an AI agent with merchant locks, amount caps, and expiry so autonomous purchases stay inside policy, a use the vendor documents by name

citations.quote: Issue cards per agent, workflow, or vendor via API. Each card closes automatically when the workflow ends.
Set velocity limits, merchant category restrictions, and per-transaction caps at the card, account, or program level. Every rule is evaluated at authorization, before funds move.
You can configure that logic on merchant category codes (MCC), dollar amount, authorization count, and more.
This creates a velocity control that enforces a weekly spending limit of $1,000.
